subject: Meteorology
title: TIROS-1: The First Weather Satellite
description: One-minute skill: TIROS-1: The First Weather Satellite.

hook.text: On April 1, 1960, TIROS-1 launched—sending back the first television images of Earth's weather patterns from space.

buildup.text: For 78 days, its two cameras captured cloud patterns over vast ocean areas never before observed by any weather station.

discovery.text: The images revealed how clouds organize on a continental scale—showing hurricanes, fronts, and vortices from above.

twist.text: Before TIROS, storms could form and intensify over open ocean completely undetected—satellites ended that blind spot.

climax.text: TIROS proved that satellite meteorology was viable—launching a revolution in global weather observation.

punchline.text: 78 days in orbit—and weather observation gained a new dimension.
